charts.annotation: Gross Revenue (IFRS line) = Net revenue + Pass-through costs. Pass-through carries no margin; all guided ratios below are on net revenue.

Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs FCF After Leases
charts.annotation: FCF after leases deducts lease principal repayments (IFRS 16). Owner FCF (DCF card above) further strips SBC and interest income.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Publicis Groupe SA: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Publicis Groupe SA: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Publicis Groupe SA: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Publicis Groupe SA: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. FCF after leases further deducts IFRS 16 lease principal repayments -- agencies lease most of their office space, so this is a more honest cash figure. Owner FCF (DCF card above) goes one step further, also stripping stock-based compensation and interest income.

For Publicis Groupe SA: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF (H1 is seasonally negative)

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Publicis Groupe SA: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Publicis Groupe SA: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Operating income is the IFRS statutory line, after one-off items such as restructuring and impairments; net income is after interest and tax.

For Publicis Groupe SA: this differs from the headline Operating Margin (EUR) card above, which is management's own non-IFRS KPI before those one-offs -- the gap between the two lines is exactly the one-off items for the year.

What to watch:

  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)
  • Statutory operating income converging with or diverging from the headline margin figure

revenue.title: Net revenue vs pass-through costs
revenue.content:
Net revenue (revenue less pass-through costs) is Publicis's headline KPI -- the number management guides to and the basis of every reported margin and organic-growth figure. Pass-through costs are media and production costs billed through to clients at no margin (mainly in programmatic/production work); gross IFRS Revenue is simply net revenue plus pass-through.

For Publicis Groupe SA: pass-through grew much faster than net revenue (+38% in FY2025), so the gross Revenue line overstates organic momentum -- the DCF is built entirely on net revenue for this reason.

What to watch:

  • Net revenue YoY (the organic-growth proxy), not gross Revenue
  • Pass-through as a rising share of gross Revenue (margin dilution, not growth)
  • Interim rows show H1/H2 seasonality

opMarginEUR.title: Headline operating margin (management KPI)
opMarginEUR.content:
Operating margin here is Publicis's own headline profitability KPI, in EUR and as a % of net revenue -- not the IFRS operating income line shown in the Profit chart, which sits after one-off items such as restructuring and impairments.

For Publicis Groupe SA: FY2025 headline operating margin was EUR 2,648m, 18.2% of net revenue -- exactly the rate management guides to and the DCF's EBITDA-margin assumption is benchmarked against.

What to watch:

  • The % trend, since the EUR figure alone mixes margin with net-revenue growth
  • Gap between this and statutory operating income (one-offs)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Publicis Groupe SA: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
